knowledge_gaps: Recent-branch computation is understated. Encoding a separate ten-item window at every supervised position can cost substantially more than two sequence encodings. Chunking forward calls alone may retain all backward graphs and fail to bound training memory; code difficulty 4 needs profiling evidence.

Positional semantics are unresolved. With learned absolute positions and left padding, a short full prefix and a reindexed recent window need not produce identical features. Reusing full features for prefixes of length at most ten requires an explicit positional convention and parity checks.

Reproducibility requires the gate architecture, prefix-length definition after baseline truncation, padding masks, recent-window position IDs, chunk/backward strategy, checkpoint-selection schedule, and GPU-budget allocation.

The proposed comparisons omit recent-only SASRec and a cheaper recency-pooling baseline. These controls would distinguish gains from truncation, fusion, and learned gating. Originality 3 is reasonable; potential 7 remains speculative without these comparisons.

The evaluation plan needs paired validation uncertainty and limits on adaptive selection. Gate saturation, branch similarity, feature norms, and performance by history length should also be measured: the gate could exploit scale or length shortcuts rather than select current intent.

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve positional inconsistencies and find a feasible implementation before assigning low implementation difficulty. A local attention mask alone does not necessarily reproduce independently truncated windows across multiple layers.
follow_up_queries.query: For SASRec with learned absolute positional embeddings, left-padded sequences, and multiple causal Transformer layers, how can independently reindexed sliding-window representations be computed at every training position? Compare explicit window batching, activation checkpointing, and local attention in terms of exact equivalence, autograd memory, and computational complexity.
